name: Rabbitproof: Spam Bot Protection
author: rabbitproof

sections.description:
Spam bots fill in website forms by themselves: junk comments, fake sign-ups, fake orders and contact form spam. Rabbitproof blocks them, and your real visitors don’t notice a thing. There are no puzzles, no ticks and nothing to click.

What it protects

  • Comments
  • Sign-ups and lost password
  • Sign-ins
  • WooCommerce checkout and account sign-ups
  • Contact Form 7
  • WPForms
  • Gravity Forms
  • Elementor forms
  • Fluent Forms

Features

  • Form spam protection
  • Comment spam protection
  • Brute force login protection
  • Fake account protection
  • Automated browser detection
  • Proxy and VPN detection
  • Multi-connection device detection
  • Repeat offender blocking
  • Shared bot blocklist
  • Direct POST protection
  • Scanner and private file blocking

Rabbitproof is free. Each website can use up to 10,000 requests a month; above that, protection pauses until the next month. You make a free Rabbitproof account when you connect. No card needed.

Need more? Bot Management for WordPress checks every visitor before they reach your website, with geoblocking, content scraping protection and origin protection.

External services

This plugin connects to Rabbitproof (rabbitproof.com.au), a service run by the plugin’s authors, to tell real visitors from spam bots. It cannot work without it. Nothing is sent to Rabbitproof, and nothing is loaded from it, until you press Connect to Rabbitproof.

What is sent, and when:

  • When a visitor views a page: a Rabbitproof script checks the visitor’s browser and connection, and Rabbitproof answers with a pass, kept in a cookie on your website. Not used on Bot Management for WordPress, where Rabbitproof checks visitors before they reach your website.
  • When a form is sent: the visitor’s IP address and browser details, the form’s address and kind, and the visitor’s pass. What the visitor typed is never sent.
  • When someone asks your website for a private file: their IP address and the address they asked for.
  • To set up protection: your website’s page and form addresses.
  • When you use the plugin’s settings, connect it or remove it: your Rabbitproof settings and your Requests list, using your website’s keys.

Service provider: Rabbitproof (rabbitproof.com.au)

  • Terms of service: https://rabbitproof.com.au/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://rabbitproof.com.au/privacy
  • Compliance, including our Data Processing Agreement: https://rabbitproof.com.au/compliance

sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open Rabbitproof in the WordPress menu and press Connect to Rabbitproof.
  3. Sign in to your Rabbitproof account, or make one. You come back to WordPress connected.
sections.faq:
Will my visitors notice?

No. There are no puzzles and nothing to click.

Does it work with my forms?

Rabbitproof works with WordPress comments, sign-ups, sign-ins and lost password, WooCommerce checkout, Contact Form 7, WPForms, Gravity Forms, Elementor forms and Fluent Forms. Each one has its own switch on the Forms tab.

What happens to a message that was blocked?

It isn’t lost. Comments go to your Spam folder. Contact form messages are kept on your website for 30 days, where you can read them and unblock the sender.

What if a real person is blocked?

It’s very unlikely. Rabbitproof checks how the whole visit behaves, not just the internet address, so real people go straight through. If it ever happens, press Unblock on the Requests tab.

Does it work with page caching?

Yes.

Is it free?

Yes. The plugin and the service are free, with no card and no trial. Each website can use up to 10,000 requests a month, which is more than most small business websites need. If a website goes over, protection pauses until the next month starts, and forms still go through.

Where can I use Rabbitproof?

Everywhere except the European Union, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, the United Kingdom and Switzerland.
sections.changelog:
1.0.74

  • Rate limiting for Bot Management for WordPress, off until you turn it on.

1.0.73

  • Rabbitproof is now free, for up to 10,000 requests a month.
  • Shorter wording in the settings and the External services section.
  • The “Can’t reach Rabbitproof” notice only shows while Rabbitproof really can’t be reached.

1.0.72

  • Updated the Bot Management for WordPress price.

1.0.71

  • New protections against scanners.
  • Clearer details in the External services section.

1.0.70

  • Better at spotting automated browsers when a form is sent.

1.0.69

  • Spam blocked now counts every spam message, and Bots blocked counts every other bot. The table under them counts the same way.
  • The Overview shows plain numbers, without percentages.
  • More room for the status in the request lists.

1.0.68

  • Rabbitproof now checks comments and every supported form before other spam plugins, so every message gets its check.
  • Clearer wording on the Protection tab.

1.0.67

  • A calmer layout: small section labels, and each section’s settings grouped together.
  • Every blocked message, comments included, shows everything that was sent, in the same layout.
  • A message only shows under its own form’s row.
  • Unblock asks in the plugin’s own pop-up.
  • View spam folder opens the right place for comments, Flamingo, Fluent Forms and Gravity Forms.
  • Bot Management: the honeypot link is its own setting, and Protect your numbered pages is now Content scraping protection.
  • Bot Management: choose the device check theme (Light, Dark or Match visitor) in the plugin.

1.0.61

  • Overview shows the spam blocked on its own card, beside the bots blocked.
  • Shares under 1% or over 99% show one decimal, so a few real people never read as 0%.
  • A scan from many addresses has the same Blocked label as every other row.

1.0.60

  • That row stands out with a solid red Blocked label.

1.0.59

  • A scan from many addresses at once shows as one row on Requests, with how many requests and addresses.

1.0.58

  • A blocked comment shows what was written and the post it was on, with a link to your spam folder.

1.0.56

  • Requests for private files get the same refusal your server gives itself.

1.0.55

  • Private files your server refuses now show on the Requests tab.
  • Repeated failed sign-ins through XML-RPC are refused, and a new switch turns XML-RPC off.

1.0.54

  • First release.
